name: Accurate data-practice disclosure
definition: Privacy statements and operational documentation must explain actual collection, purposes, recipients, storage, controls and responsibilities.
inclusion: Missing or stale policies, misleading claims, undocumented SDK behavior, and explanations of privacy-related settings or tools.
exclusion: Use B when the content exists but cannot be found or read; C for choosing permission, and S for broader compliance planning.

name: Accessible privacy information and controls
definition: Users need to find, read and operate privacy notices and controls across layouts, languages and assistive technologies.
inclusion: Broken links, missing notice placement, translations, clipped or obscured controls, contrast, navigation and responsive-layout failures.
exclusion: Use A for substantive disclosure accuracy, D for stored choice errors, and R for broader application breakage under protection.

name: Meaningful and purpose-specific choice
definition: Data use or publication requires an understandable user choice whose default, granularity, timing and withdrawal match the intended purpose.
inclusion: Opt-in versus opt-out, equal rejection, granular permissions, confirmation before publication, contact preferences and misleading action labels.
exclusion: Use F for telemetry-specific collection decisions; D for state/audit implementation and E for enforcing a choice on processing.

name: Reliable consent state and audit trail
definition: Consent must be represented, retained, revised and evidenced consistently through navigation, identity changes, scopes and policy revisions.
inclusion: Lost or conflicting consent cookies, repeated prompts, broken persistence, versioned acceptance records and re-consent.
exclusion: Use E for downstream enforcement or vendor/purpose propagation; a required checkbox alone is not an audit record.

name: Consent-aware processing and propagation
definition: Data-processing components must receive and honor applicable permission before and after changes in user choice.
inclusion: Deferred initialization, tracking/script gating, consent strings, vendor and purpose rules, cross-component propagation and withdrawal enforcement.
exclusion: Use D for persistence within a choice store, F for general telemetry policy and R for functionality that breaks because protection is effective.

name: Bounded and controllable telemetry
definition: Usage, diagnostic or behavioral measurement needs justified scope, understandable defaults and effective collection controls.
inclusion: Telemetry introduction/removal, opt-in defaults, opt-out ignored, scoped metrics, identifiers and data previews.
exclusion: Use J for sensitive diagnostic payloads or publication, G for nontelemetry minimization, and E for general consent-component plumbing.

name: Data minimization and local persistence
definition: Collect or persist only information necessary for the stated function, at the required granularity and location.
inclusion: Unnecessary account fields, preinteraction cookies, localStorage alternatives, behavioral trails, memory-only storage and avoiding needless identifiers.
exclusion: Use L for expiry of already retained data, I for transformation of identifiers, and H for external recipients or services.

name: Control over external services and requests
definition: Optional integrations, embedded resources and external processing must not create unexamined disclosure or dependence on third parties.
inclusion: Remote fonts, maps, favicons, link previews, updater calls, local/self-hosted alternatives, provider choice and data-region constraints.
exclusion: Use F for intentional telemetry, N for a concrete unintended recipient/content leak, and O for transport encryption itself.

name: Effective de-identification
definition: Masking, pseudonymization, aggregation or metadata removal must cover relevant fields and representations while preserving necessary utility.
inclusion: Incomplete scrubbing, indirect identifiers, stable mapping, export anonymization, spatial/time coarsening, synthetic replacements and operational failures of scrubbers.
exclusion: Use J for diagnostic-specific redaction, K for erasure, P for resource permission and Q for fingerprint defenses; pseudonymization is not assumed irreversible anonymity.

name: Safe diagnostic collection and sharing
definition: Logs, error reports and support artifacts need sensitive-data filtering, appropriate destinations and review before disclosure.
inclusion: Credentials, identifying URLs or personal data in logs, safe logging defaults, synthetic reproductions and private/pre-upload diagnostic inspection.
exclusion: Use F for whether telemetry is collected, I for non-diagnostic de-identification, and L for retention duration alone.

name: Complete and usable erasure
definition: Removing data requires an accessible request/action and coverage of related, derived, cached or distributed records within the supported scope.
inclusion: Account deletion, forgotten uploads, residual indexes/history, deletion versus deactivation, identity unlinking and erasure propagation.
exclusion: Use L for automatic age limits, I for retaining transformed records, T for access/export; local erasure does not prove removal of external copies.

name: Bounded retention and expiry
definition: Stored data needs an appropriate lifetime and cleanup process that respects operational and evidentiary constraints.
inclusion: Timed log/cache/post deletion, inactive-account cleanup, retention configuration and preserving necessary audit or transaction records.
exclusion: Use K for specific erasure actions and their completeness; use A when only retention wording changes.

name: Context-appropriate access and visibility
definition: Who can discover, view or act on information must match role, account, tenant, audience and contextual sharing boundaries.
inclusion: Private profiles, role permissions, enumeration, search/index visibility, contextual enrollment and identity-sensitive audience selection.
exclusion: Use N for concrete wrong-recipient or unintended-output incidents, C for user agreement itself, and O for credential/cryptographic mechanisms.

name: Prevention of unintended disclosure
definition: Information must not escape through an unintended recipient, context, surface or inherited state.
inclusion: Wrong-recipient messages, cross-account collisions, exposed private URL/data, notification contents, shared-screen traces and accidental secret publication.
exclusion: Use M for general audience/access design, J for diagnostic payloads and H for intentional external-service architecture.

name: Confidentiality and authentication safeguards
definition: Encryption, key handling, secure transport and authentication mechanisms must protect sensitive content and credentials under the relevant threat model.
inclusion: Field/database encryption, TLS, key exchange, credential storage/reveal, session protection and account recovery.
exclusion: Use M for authorization/audience policies; general integrity work without a privacy connection belongs in U.

name: Appropriate sensitive-resource permissions
definition: Access to device/browser capabilities must be necessary, correctly declared and understandable, with deliberate activation and suitable scope.
inclusion: Microphone, camera, contacts, location, sensor or privacy-settings permissions, least privilege and platform declaration failures.
exclusion: Use C for non-platform consent, Q for fingerprinting, and E where a privacy action fails to stop transmission.

name: Resistance to identification and linkability
definition: Observable identifiers, timing or platform behavior must not unintentionally allow identification or correlation beyond the intended scope.
inclusion: Browser/API fingerprinting, identifying headers, anonymous transaction sets, cross-context identifiers and privacy-preserving linkage designs.
exclusion: Use I for data-set de-identification, M for directory enumeration and H for third-party network architecture.

name: Functionality under privacy constraints
definition: Software must handle restricted storage, blocked tracking, masked environment information or privacy-oriented dependencies without breaking required functionality.
inclusion: Tracking protection compatibility, blocked-cookie authentication, masked timezone/OS, privacy component performance and privacy-related API/provider migration.
exclusion: Use B for notice/control layout, D for consent-state bugs, and E for failing to enforce rather than tolerate a restriction.

name: Actionable privacy governance
definition: Teams translate privacy obligations and risks into scoped requirements, reviews, ownership, operational procedures or incident-response support.
inclusion: Compliance readiness, data inventory, children/jurisdiction requirements, processor review, standards alignment, breach templates and private reporting channels.
exclusion: Do not treat participant legal claims or checklists as certification; use a specific technical code when that is the principal concern.

name: Usable personal-data access and export
definition: Users or operators need appropriately scoped access, copies or portable records of personal data and associated requests.
inclusion: Readable chat/data export, access requests, portability, authorized submission receipts and distinguishing access from erasure.
exclusion: Use I for privacy transformation of exports, M for access restrictions and K for erasure.

name: Privacy claim not established by available material
definition: The supplied record does not substantiate a specific privacy issue, or explicitly corrects an initial privacy allegation.
inclusion: Vague complaints, irrelevant privacy mentions, withdrawn accusations, false-positive alerts and ordinary technical behavior with no demonstrated privacy mechanism.
exclusion: Use substantive concern codes for supported requests even if unimplemented; this category retains the case without manufacturing a privacy defect.
